name: Brendyn Beasley
tagline: I take the papers that built economics and *ask again.*
lede: {studies} studies so far. Each one starts from a result that shaped the field, rebuilds its test from public data and reports what still holds.

about.statement: I study economics and statistics at the University of Minnesota. My work starts with a question someone has already answered. I take a paper that shaped the field, rebuild its test from public data, and see whether the answer *still holds.*
about.note: So far that is {replications} replications, from Cournot's {firstYear} theory of competition to papers published in {lastYear}, plus original work on how wet years reshape Minnesota's county economies. Each replication ships with its data, its code, a technical companion and a write-up in plain English.

capabilities.title: Replicate
capabilities.text: Rebuild a published result from its original sources, then extend it with data the authors never had: Census tables, SEC filings, FRED series, Medicare records, 88 million eBay listings.

capabilities.title: Estimate
capabilities.text: Panel regressions with fixed effects, instrumental variables, event studies, bootstrapped intervals and placebo tests, chosen to fit the question and not the other way round.

capabilities.title: Explain
capabilities.text: Every study is written to be read: one question, the real numbers, a section on why it matters and a section on its limits.

capabilities.title: Build
capabilities.text: Design and ship interactive tools that run in a browser: study apps, a paper archive, a county-level research dashboard.
